basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Bibensque vinum inebriatus est, et nudatus in tabernaculo suo. Bibit vinum Dominus cum'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Bibensque vinum inebriatus est, et nudatus in tabernaculo suo. Bibit vinum Dominus cum calicem passionis accepit. Inebriatus est bibendo, cum patiendo pro nobis usque ad mortis extrema pervenit. Nudatus est in tabernaculo suo, cum in populo Judaeorum, quem suum fecerat proprium, et in quo jam dudum velut in tabernaculo suo manere consueverat, probra irrisionesque sustinens, ad ultimum crucis patibulum subiit, manifestissime omnibus patefaciens veritatem substantiae mortalis quam suscipere dignatus est.
